complexity_scope.guarantee: Expectation over Algorithm and environment randomness, including adaptive environments allowed by §2.
complexity_scope.hidden_constants: The displayed bound is explicit: coefficient 4 and additive constant 1; no asymptotic hidden factor is introduced.
complexity_scope.oracle: One selected-arm loss observation per round.
complexity_scope.output_and_metric: Online sampled actions; pseudo-regret E[sum_t ell_t,I_t]-min_i E[sum_t ell_t,i]. No final-arm recommendation guarantee.
complexity_scope.regime: All integers K>=2 and T>=1 under the stated bounded-loss adversarial model; anytime learning rate.
complexity_scope.resource: T selected-arm observations; separately charge T regularized simplex optimizations, T categorical draws and state/estimator computation. The bound does not give total runtime or finite-precision complexity.
complexity_scope.upper_witness_or_lower_coverage: The selected exact symmetric half-Tsallis Algorithm with IW estimators, fully specified in the statement; no claim over unrestricted Algorithms.

content.intended_use: A selected Algorithm upper bound for adversarial bandit pseudo-regret with explicit constants.

proofs.locator: PDF p.18 equation (6); p.20 Lemma 11 part 1 and Lemma 12 part 1; p.21 §7.3 opening paragraph; p.24 Proof of Theorem 3
map: Equation (6), p.18, decomposes pseudo-regret into expected stability and penalty terms using Phi_t=(-Psi_t conjugation with the simplex constraint), written in the paper as Phi_t=(Psi_t+I_Delta)^*.

The opening of Proof of Theorem 1, p.21, explicitly omits the IW proofs and says that the adversarial IW argument is analogous to Proof of Theorem 3. This record preserves that source-provided route rather than claiming a printed complete IW proof.
Lemma 11 part 1, p.20, bounds instantaneous stability for IW, any positive eta_t and alpha in [0,1], by min{sum_i (eta_t xi_i/2) E[w_t,i]^(1-alpha),1}.
Lemma 12 part 1, p.20, bounds total penalty for symmetric regularization and non-increasing positive rates by ((K^(1-alpha)-1)(1-T^(-alpha)))/((1-alpha)alpha eta_T)+1.

Proof of Theorem 3, p.24, uses equation (6), the IW stability bound, maximization over the simplex, time summation and the symmetric penalty bound. These are the source-located ingredients to which the paper directs the adversarial IW reader. Its general-alpha tuned learning rate must not be silently substituted for the Theorem 1 schedule.
proofs.omitted_details: The original explicitly omits the dedicated IW proof. Appendix C proofs of the stability and penalty lemmas were not read in this job. No reconstructed local proof or local transfer claim is supplied; this is a faithful literature Proof map, not independent reproof.
proofs.reading_coverage: Actually inspected the listed anchors and their original-page JPEG formulas/layout on pp.18,20,21,24, together with the statement/specification on pp.5,7–9. Did not read the complete self-bounding proof or Appendix C.

assumptions: The adversary may select losses using past actions and its internal randomness, as in §2; losses cannot depend on the current sampled action.
Use Algorithm 1 with IW estimators, alpha=1/2, symmetric xi_i=1, eta_t=2/sqrt(t), zero cumulative-estimate initialization and exact regularized predictions.
statement.objects_and_definitions: There are K arms. At round t, ell_t belongs to [0,1]^K and only ell_t,I_t is observed and incurred. Delta is the probability simplex. Define Rbar_T=E[sum_(t=1)^T ell_t,I_t]-min_(i=1,...,K) E[sum_(t=1)^T ell_t,i]. A comparator i*_T is an arm minimizing the latter expectation. Set Lhat_0=0, Psi(w)=-4 sum_i sqrt(w_i)+2 sum_i w_i and eta_t=2/sqrt(t). At each round compute the exact w_t=argmin_(w in Delta){<w,Lhat_(t-1)>+Psi(w)/eta_t}, sample I_t from w_t, form ellhat_t,i=1{I_t=i}ell_t,I_t/w_t,i, and update Lhat_t=Lhat_(t-1)+ellhat_t.
statement.parameter_domains: K in integers >=2; T in integers >=1; t=1,...,T; alpha=1/2; xi_i=1 for all arms; eta_t=2/sqrt(t). No unique-best-arm, gap or self-bounding assumption is needed for this adversarial branch.
statement.quantifiers_and_randomness: For every integer K>=2, every integer T>=1, and every adversarial bandit environment satisfying these conditions, the specified Algorithm satisfies the bound. Expectations include the internal randomness of both the Algorithm and environment. The minimum is outside the expectation; this is not an adaptive-adversary expected hindsight-regret or high-probability statement.
